headline: Single EOA proxy owner with upgrade, mint/issue, and role-management powers; no timelock or multisig on T1 path

findings.text: Token proxy owner() at 0x7712c34205737192402172409a8F7ccef8aA2AEc returns 0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e (https://defipunkd.com/api/contract/read?chainId=1&address=0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec&method=owner, block 25237812). Etherscan confirms 0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e is an EOA that has performed token issuance and bridge management for BUIDL[](https://etherscan.io/address/0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e).

0x7712c34205737192402172409a8F7ccef8aA2AEc is an upgradeable proxy (implementation 0x603Bb6909Be14f83282E03632280D91bE7fB83b2). Etherscan and defipunkd surfacer confirm proxy pattern with upgradeTo/upgradeToAndCall capability in the verified implementation (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec; https://etherscan.io/address/0x603Bb6909Be14f83282E03632280D91bE7fB83b2).

No multisig or timelock surfaced for the proxy owner or token admin roles. Control is held by single EOA 0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e[](https://etherscan.io/address/0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e). Contract uses role-based access (ROLE_MASTER, TOKEN_ISSUER, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE, TRANSFER_AGENT etc.) grantable by owner[](https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec).

Highest tier reachable on uncontested path is T1: EOA can replace implementation (upgradeTo), mint/issue shares (evidenced by past issuance txs), change accounting/compliance logic, and manage roles that gate transfers and issuance. No timelock or multi-sig gate (https://etherscan.io/address/0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e; proxy surfacer evidence).

steelman.red: Single EOA holds proxy ownership with direct upgrade, issuance, and role-grant powers and no timelock or Security Council; T1 blast radius (implementation swap or unbacked mint) is reachable in one transaction.
steelman.orange: Complex role-based compliance system (TRANSFER_AGENT, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE) and verified implementation provide some operational guardrails; on-chain actions are logged and limited to whitelisted flows.
steelman.green: Token is a representation of off-chain Treasury/repo assets; on-chain admin powers cannot directly drain on-chain user funds or alter underlying custody (which sits with BNY Mellon/BlackRock).

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because the uncontested fast path gives a single EOA T1 powers (upgrade + mint/issue + role admin) with zero delay or multi-party check; steelman for red is materially stronger than orange/green given the explicit EOA owner and proxy upgrade surface.

evidence.shows: owner() returns the EOA 0xe01605f6b6dC593b7d2917F4a0940db2A625b09e at block 25237812; proves admin control surface
Proxy to implementation 0x603Bb6909Be14f83282E03632280D91bE7fB83b2; role constants and upgrade events (ProxyTargetSet, ProxyOwnerChanged); isPaused false; confirms upgradeable + role-based control
EOA (no contract code); historical token issuance to BUIDL contract and bridge management txs; confirms single-party admin actor
Verified DSToken implementation with Ownable, upgradeTo/upgradeToAndCall, initialize, and role-based patterns; confirms T1 upgrade surface reachable by proxy owner

unknowns: C3: No timelock or queued execution path found; execution is direct owner call (no MIN_DELAY or queue contract surfaced).
C4: No Gnosis Safe or multisig owners/thresholds found for admin roles; only EOA surfaced. Other chains' token owners not read.
C5: No on-chain Governor or token-weighted governance contract found.
C6: Emergency pause/guardian role exists in role system but actor holding PAUSE/guardian and time cap not read on-chain this run.

admin_addresses.role: proxy owner / token owner (EOA admin with issuance, upgrade, role-grant powers)

headline: On-chain token transfers possible between whitelisted holders; full cash redemption requires off-chain Transfer Agent process with deadlines and issuer cooperation
short_headline: Platform-mediated exit; no permissionless on-chain redeem

findings.text: User-facing exit paths: on-chain transfer() / transferFrom() to whitelisted addresses (24/7 P2P); off-chain redemption request to Transfer Agent (Securitize) for USD settlement. No direct user-facing burn/redeem/claim function for cash on main token contract (https://securitize.io/blackrock/buidl; https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec).

On-chain transfer is gated by compliance/whitelist roles (TRANSFER_AGENT, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE, WALLET_REGISTRAR). Off-chain redemption requires submitting request to Transfer Agent during business hours; on-chain token movement to their wallet must finalize before settlement[](https://securitize.io/blackrock/buidl).

isPaused() currently false on token proxy (surfacer data). Contract has pause/unpause capability via roles; no on-chain evidence of infinite-pause cap or actor this run. Pause would block transfers but redemption queue is off-chain.
Redemption requests have daily cut-off (8am-3pm ET) for same-day settlement; missed deadline rolls to next day. No documented on-chain queue or daily withdrawal cap for token itself.
On-chain transfers are directly callable via any wallet/SDK on verified contract (no frontend dependency for P2P transfer). Full USD exit requires Securitize platform/Transfer Agent cooperation.

steelman.red: No permissionless on-chain function to redeem BUIDL for USD or underlying Treasuries; exit to cash depends entirely on issuer/Transfer Agent process, deadlines, and whitelist status; admin-controlled pause or role revocation can block even on-chain liquidity.
steelman.orange: On-chain P2P transfers between whitelisted holders are permissionless and 24/7; daily dividend tokens accrue automatically; redemption process is documented, time-bounded per business day, and uses regulated transfer agent.
steelman.green: Token itself is transferable on-chain without admin signature once whitelisted; 'instant' redemption marketing and same-day settlement window provide practical exit for compliant users.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because there is no on-chain exit function that lets a user unilaterally convert tokens to USD/principal without issuer cooperation; the operative exit path is off-chain and gated by Transfer Agent deadlines and whitelist status. Steelman for red outweighs orange/green.

evidence.shows: Redemptions processed via Transfer Agent with 8am-3pm ET window for same-day settlement; on-chain transfers 24/7 to whitelisted investors only; daily dividends paid as new BUIDL tokens; Qualified Purchaser + min $5M; confirms off-chain exit dependency
Token proxy with role-based access control (TRANSFER_AGENT, COMPLIANCE_SERVICE, etc.); isPaused false; upgradeable; confirms on-chain transfer gating and lack of public redeem function
Verified proxy + implementation; security token profile; no public redeem/burn interface listed for retail exit

unknowns: E2: Exact on-chain modifiers or hasRole checks for transfer vs. redeem/burn not read this run (method-isPaused failed; full ABI enumeration incomplete).
E3: Actor holding pause/guardian role and maximum pause duration not determined on-chain.
E4: No evidence of separate emergency vs governance pause paths; role system implies issuer-controlled pause.
E6: No permissionless emergency-exit or escape-hatch function found for adversarial-admin scenario.

headline: Fully dependent on BlackRock (asset mgr), BNY Mellon (custodian), Securitize (transfer agent + KYC whitelist) and off-chain Treasuries/repo; ~100% TVS at risk from TradFi counterparty failure
short_headline: TradFi RWA dependencies; no on-chain fallback

findings.text: Core token contract has no on-chain oracles, AMMs, or lending pools it calls. All pricing/NAV, yield accrual, and collateral (Treasuries/repo) are off-chain and managed by BlackRock. Token only tracks ownership and enables whitelisted transfers (https://securitize.io/blackrock/buidl; https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec).

Off-chain actor committees: BlackRock (portfolio manager), BNY Mellon (custodian per RWA.xyz data), Securitize (transfer agent, KYC/AML whitelist manager, redemption processor). Mis-reporting or failure by any can freeze redemptions or impair token value/peg. No on-chain validator set or slashing.

Multi-chain deployments (Ethereum primary + Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Polygon, Solana, Aptos, BNB) inherit canonical bridges or platform-specific messaging. No material TVL on non-canonical bridges identified; primary risk is operational coordination across chains by Securitize.
No nested restaking/LRT; underlying is traditional short-term Treasuries and overnight repo held in custody. Failure at custody or asset-manager level directly impairs share value.
No on-chain circuit breakers, sanity-check oracles, or fallback mechanisms for external TradFi failures. Yield is paid in new tokens daily; redemption queue is off-chain only.
Proxy owner EOA can upgrade implementation and change roles (including compliance/transfer-agent roles). No evidence of on-chain timelock protecting users from silent dependency swaps.

steelman.red: 100% of TVS depends on off-chain BlackRock asset management, BNY Mellon custody, and Securitize operational/KYC infrastructure; no on-chain fallback or recoverable path if any TradFi counterparty fails or withholds cooperation.
steelman.orange: Token itself is simple ownership ledger with whitelisted P2P transfers; daily dividends auto-accrue on-chain; regulated entities (BlackRock, BNYM, Securitize) provide institutional operational resilience and legal recourse.
steelman.green: BUIDL is a direct claim on high-quality, liquid short-term Treasuries/repo with BlackRock's balance sheet and regulatory oversight; on-chain token layer adds minimal additional dependency beyond standard RWA custody.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because every critical path (yield generation, custody, redemption finality, whitelist maintenance) is external TradFi with no on-chain mitigation or fallback; impacted TVS is effectively 100%. Steelman for red is decisively stronger.

evidence.shows: Core investments are off-chain overnight repo and 3-month Treasuries; BlackRock manages the fund; Securitize is transfer agent and platform for KYC/whitelisting/subscriptions/redemptions; confirms full TradFi dependency stack
Custodian: Bank of New York Mellon; Transfer Agent & Paying Agent: Securitize; Issuer domiciled British Virgin Islands; confirms external counterparty dependencies
Token contract performs no external contract calls to oracles, bridges, or yield sources; purely ownership + role-gated transfer ledger

unknowns: A1: Exact external contract calls (if any) from implementation not fully enumerated due to ABI gaps on proxy reads.
A7: Multi-chain sequencer/bridge liveness dependencies not assessed per-chain beyond primary Ethereum deployment.
A8: Keeper/relayer dependencies for off-chain processes (dividend distribution, redemption settlement) not on-chain visible.

headline: Contract and platform enforce KYC/AML whitelist; only Qualified Purchasers with $5M+ minimum; transfers restricted to approved wallets; no independent permissionless access path
short_headline: KYC-whitelisted security token; min $5M QP only

findings.text: Token contract uses role-based modifiers (COMPLIANCE_SERVICE, TRANSFER_AGENT, WALLET_REGISTRAR, TOKEN_ISSUER) that gate transfers and issuance. Transfers only permitted to whitelisted investors (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec; https://securitize.io/blackrock/buidl).
Off-chain operators in admission path: Securitize KYC/AML team and Transfer Agent control whitelist and approve subscriptions/redemptions. No permissionless on-chain admission for new users.

Frontend (Securitize platform) enforces Qualified Purchaser status, sanctions attestation, and jurisdiction restrictions. Active runtime enforcement via KYC wall and whitelist. ToS and platform UI restrict access to eligible investors only.

No published SDK, third-party frontend, wallet integration, or aggregator routing that bypasses Securitize KYC/whitelist for new admissions. On-chain transfers possible only after whitelist approval via official platform.
On-chain blocklist/whitelist enforcement via roles; contract does not accept arbitrary addresses for meaningful participation (transfer/holding).
Read access (view balance, transfers) is permissionless on verified contract. Write access (transfer, receive meaningful value) is gated to whitelisted addresses.
Securitize ToS and platform require KYC/AML, Qualified Purchaser certification, and compliance with applicable law. Verbatim eligibility language present on https://securitize.io/blackrock/buidl.

steelman.red: Admission to any economically meaningful use (holding, transferring, subscribing, redeeming) requires off-chain KYC/AML approval and Qualified Purchaser status via Securitize; contract enforces whitelist at transfer level; no independent access path exists.
steelman.orange: Once whitelisted, on-chain P2P transfers are permissionless 24/7 between approved wallets; read state is fully open; regulated platform provides compliant on-ramp for eligible institutions.
steelman.green: Token contract itself has no hardcoded geographic or single-party gate beyond role-managed compliance; any whitelisted user can transfer freely without further admin approval per transaction.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because both contract-level (role-gated transfers) and platform-level (KYC wall + QP + $5M min) barriers exist, and no credible independent access path bypasses the official Securitize onboarding. Steelman for red is strongest.

evidence.shows: Qualified Purchaser status required for Ethereum and several chains; minimum investment $5M; 'only permits token transfers to whitelisted investors'; KYC/AML standards enforced; subscription/redemption via Securitize platform only
Role-based access control with COMPLIANCE_SERVICE, TRANSFER_AGENT, WALLET_REGISTRAR, TOKEN_ISSUER; confirms on-chain whitelist/transfer gating
Security token profile; verified proxy with compliance features; no open mint/transfer for arbitrary addresses

unknowns: A1: Full list of functions protected by onlyRole or whitelist modifiers not exhaustively read due to ABI resolution limits on proxy.
A3b: Existence of any third-party SDK, CLI, or aggregator that routes new users without Securitize KYC not confirmed (searches returned none).

headline: Proxy and implementation bytecode verified Exact Match on Etherscan with source visible; no public GitHub repo or recognized-firm audit found; automated scan exists but insufficient for green
short_headline: Etherscan verified; missing public repo + recognized audit

findings.text: Proxy 0x7712c34205737192402172409a8F7ccef8aA2AEc and implementation 0x603Bb6909Be14f83282E03632280D91bE7fB83b2 both have verified source on Etherscan (Exact Match). defipunkd surfacer confirms ABI from etherscan/sourcify and proxy resolution (https://defipunkd.com/address/1/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec; https://etherscan.io/token/0x7712c34205737192402172409a8f7ccef8aa2aec).
Source code is visible on Etherscan for both proxy and DSToken implementation. No matching public GitHub repository or commit SHA found in searches or pinned context.

No audit links in per-protocol context. Searches surfaced one automated security scan by Veritas Protocol (average score) and mentions of internal/partner reviews for Arbitrum deployment; no recognized-firm (Trail of Bits, Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, etc.) audit report covering current deployment.
Veritas Protocol automated scan is not a recognized manual audit firm per rubric. No other auditor names surfaced.
Proxy is verified and correctly points to verified implementation. No unverified implementation gap.

steelman.red: No public source repository and no recognized-firm audit; contracts are institutional security tokens with complex role/compliance logic that benefits from independent review.
steelman.orange: Bytecode is fully verified Exact Match on Etherscan with source code readable; implementation is a standard Ownable + proxy pattern; some partner review occurred for chain expansions.
steelman.green: Both proxy and implementation are verified on a major explorer with source available; token is simple ownership ledger with no hidden logic; on-chain state (owner, paused, supply) is publicly readable by anyone.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because bytecode verification + visible Etherscan source satisfies part of V1/V2 but absence of public repo corresponding to deployed source and lack of any recognized-firm audit prevent green. Orange steelman is strongest match to evidence.

evidence.shows: Proxy resolved to implementation; ABI sourced from Etherscan; verification status positive; role and state reads available
Proxy and implementation source verified Exact Match; compiler details and source code accessible on explorer; no audit submitted to Etherscan
Implementation (DSToken) verified with source and Ownable/proxy patterns visible

unknowns: V2: No commit SHA or public repo URL found that matches the Etherscan-visible source; cannot confirm exact source-to-repo correspondence.
V3: No recognized-firm audit report URL or date covering the currently deployed contracts (only automated scan and internal mentions surfaced).
V5: Post-audit drift cannot be assessed without repo or audit commit pins.
